description: Capture the remaining two drift items: (a) a least-privilege memory data-plane IAM statement on the AgentCore execution role scoped to the memory ARN produced by FEAT-001; and (b) the JWT inbound authorizer config for the toolkit-managed runtime as typed, documented CDK config consumed by the deploy path (the runtime is NOT modeled in CDK). Depends on FEAT-001 (needs memory.memoryArn).
steps: In infra/lib/iam-construct.ts, add `memoryArn: string` to IamConstructProps with a JSDoc comment (ARN of the AgentCore Memory from MemoryConstruct).

In iam-construct.ts, after the existing 'CloudWatchLogs' statement, add a new iam.PolicyStatement with sid 'AgentCoreMemoryAccess', effect ALLOW, actions EXACTLY ['bedrock-agentcore:CreateEvent','bedrock-agentcore:ListEvents','bedrock-agentcore:GetEvent','bedrock-agentcore:RetrieveMemoryRecords','bedrock-agentcore:ListMemoryRecords','bedrock-agentcore:GetMemoryRecord'], resources [props.memoryArn, `${props.memoryArn}/*`]. Add a comment that this mirrors the live inline policy AgentCoreMemoryAccess and is least-privilege (no bedrock-agentcore:* wildcard, no '*' resource).
In infra/lib/production-hardening-stack.ts, pass memoryArn: memory.memoryArn into the existing IamConstruct props (the `memory` const created in FEAT-001).

Create infra/lib/runtime-auth-config.ts: export interface RuntimeJwtAuthorizerConfig { allowedClients: string[]; discoveryUrl: string } and a helper function buildCustomJwtAuthorizer(region: string, userPoolId: string, clientId: string): { customJWTAuthorizer: RuntimeJwtAuthorizerConfig } returning { customJWTAuthorizer: { allowedClients: [clientId], discoveryUrl: `https://cognito-idp.${region}.amazonaws.com/${userPoolId}/.well-known/openid-configuration` } }. Add a file-level comment: the AgentCore runtime is created by bedrock-agentcore-starter-toolkit (deploy.sh), not modeled in this CDK app; this typed config documents the inbound authorizer deploy.sh applies at launch so a from-scratch deploy reproduces it.

In production-hardening-stack.ts, import buildCustomJwtAuthorizer, build the value from props.region, userPool.userPoolId, userPoolClient.userPoolClientId, and emit it via cdk.CfnOutput 'RuntimeJwtAuthorizer' (value = JSON.stringify of the config), exportName `${props.environment}-runtime-jwt-authorizer`.
Do not add a CfnRuntime/Runtime resource; do not touch deploy.sh or .bedrock_agentcore.yaml; do not refactor unrelated constructs.
acceptance_criteria: `cd infra && npm run build` compiles with no TypeScript errors.
`cd infra && npx cdk synth` succeeds for both stacks.

cdk.out shows an IAM policy statement sid 'AgentCoreMemoryAccess' with exactly the six bedrock-agentcore data-plane actions, Resource = the memory ARN and ARN/* (a Ref/Fn::GetAtt to the memory, NOT '*'), and NO 'bedrock-agentcore:*'.
cdk.out shows a CfnOutput containing customJWTAuthorizer with allowedClients (the Cognito client id ref) and a discoveryUrl ending in /.well-known/openid-configuration.
No package.json dependency versions were changed; no CfnRuntime resource was added.
verification: ! grep -R "bedrock-agentcore:\\*" cdk.out/ (NO broad wildcard on the memory statement)
git -C infra diff --exit-code package.json (no version changes)
findings: Implemented. (a) infra/lib/iam-construct.ts: added `memoryArn: string` (JSDoc) to IamConstructProps and a new iam.PolicyStatement sid 'AgentCoreMemoryAccess' (Statement 6, placed immediately after the 'CloudWatchLogs' statement) with EXACTLY the six data-plane actions [CreateEvent, ListEvents, GetEvent, RetrieveMemoryRecords, ListMemoryRecords, GetMemoryRecord] and resources [props.memoryArn, `${props.memoryArn}/*`]; comment notes it mirrors the live inline policy and is least-privilege (no bedrock-agentcore:* , no '*'). (b) New file infra/lib/runtime-auth-config.ts exports interface RuntimeJwtAuthorizerConfig { allowedClients: string[]; discoveryUrl: string } and buildCustomJwtAuthorizer(region, userPoolId, clientId) returning { customJWTAuthorizer: { allowedClients: [clientId], discoveryUrl: https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<userPoolId>/.well-known/openid-configuration } }; file-level comment states the runtime is toolkit-managed (deploy.sh), not modeled in CDK. (c) production-hardening-stack.ts: passes `memoryArn: memory.memoryArn` into the existing IamConstruct props; imports buildCustomJwtAuthorizer; emits CfnOutput 'RuntimeJwtAuthorizer' (value = JSON.stringify of the config built from props.region, userPool.userPoolId, userPoolClient.userPoolClientId) with exportName `${props.environment}-runtime-jwt-authorizer`. No CfnRuntime/Runtime resource added; deploy.sh and .bedrock_agentcore.yaml untouched; package.json unchanged. Verification PASSED (cwd=infra): npm run build (tsc exit 0), npx cdk synth (both ProductionHardening-Staging and -Production). In both synthesized templates the AgentCoreMemoryAccess statement Resource is a Fn::GetAtt [MemoryConstructFinancialAdvisorMemory..., MemoryArn] plus the ARN/* join (NOT '*'); greps matched AgentCoreMemoryAccess, RetrieveMemoryRecords, GetMemoryRecord, customJWTAuthorizer, well-known/openid-configuration. NO 'bedrock-agentcore:*' in either *.template.json (the only match for that pattern is in the gitignored build artifact cdk.out/lib/iam-construct.js, inside the explanatory comment text, not in CFN). NO AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime in cdk.out. Note for integration: the authorizer config is CfnOutput-only (documentation/reference) — deploy.sh is what actually applies the inbound JWT authorizer at runtime launch; CDK does not provision the runtime.
